purpose: Define the bridge from Human Infra research domains to quantitative model candidate variables. The bridge prevents domains, route narratives, reviewed artifacts or enabling-resource discussions from being silently promoted into coefficients, causal effects, calibrated predictions or individual advice.

currentDecision.reason: The bridge can name where a domain could enter a future model, but it does not estimate parameters, assert causal effects, calibrate against real cohorts or support individual use.

bridgeLevels.name: domain-only
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: A domain may be listed as part of the Human Infra possibility-space map.

bridgeLevels.name: reviewed-evidence-anchor
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: A domain may point to bounded reviewed artifacts, source cards, claim evidence rows or downgrade triggers.

bridgeLevels.name: model-candidate-variable
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: A domain may be represented as a candidate state variable, intervention family, observation process, time-accounting channel, action-policy input, access probability, option-value component, governance boundary or uncertainty channel.

bridgeLevels.name: synthetic-scenario-input
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: A candidate may enter synthetic toy scenarios only when the scenario file, model card and output explicitly label it synthetic and uncalibrated.

bridgeLevels.name: aggregate-calibrated-input
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: Blocked until governed data access, exact field confirmation, extraction, disclosure review, validation and calibration diagnostics exist.

bridgeLevels.name: individual-use
bridgeLevels.allowedUse: Blocked by default in this repository.

modelLocations.meaning: A domain changes or describes the subject state X_t, such as biological condition, cognitive capacity, resource state or environment.
A domain describes an action A_t, technology, treatment, tool, policy or practice that may alter the next state or observation process.
A domain may affect P(X_{t+1} | X_t, A_t), such as repair rate, decline rate, recovery rate or learning rate.
A domain may affect lambda(t | X_t, A_t), including mortality, catastrophic failure, disease onset or acute risk.
A domain may affect what can be measured, detected, verified or monitored before a decision is made.
A domain may affect calendar time, effective time, subjective time, relative/proper time or waiting cost.
A domain may affect decision quality, attention, executive control, learning, adherence, prioritization or task selection.
A domain may affect whether the subject can discover, afford, reach, understand, adopt or persist with an intervention.
A domain may affect future choice sets, reversibility, waiting value, opportunity cost or possibility-space expansion.
A domain may affect what outputs, claims, data flows, public releases or uses are permitted.
A domain may identify uncertainty, bias, transfer limits, missingness, measurement error or downgrade conditions.

bridgeGates.name: Domain path and tier
bridgeGates.passCondition: domainPath exists in the repository and tier matches the possibility-space classification.

bridgeGates.name: Model location
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row names a valid modelLocation and explains how the domain enters the life-path model without producing a coefficient.

bridgeGates.name: Mechanism statement
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row states the domain-to-variable-to-state/risk/time/access mechanism without claiming a quantified effect.

bridgeGates.name: Measurement proxy
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row identifies observable proxy fields, instruments, registries, biomarkers, survey items or governance artifacts that could later be checked.

bridgeGates.name: Endpoint or outcome family
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row names the outcome family it could inform, such as survival, healthspan, effective time, future option value, adoption probability, calibration quality or governance safety.

bridgeGates.name: Causal status
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row distinguishes causal hypothesis, association, mechanism, measurement, access/gating or governance boundary.

bridgeGates.name: Downgrade trigger
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row declares what evidence failure, transfer issue or safety boundary would downgrade or block the candidate.

bridgeGates.name: Prohibited-use boundary
bridgeGates.passCondition: The row explicitly blocks coefficients, causal effects, calibrated prediction, medical advice, intervention ranking and individual death-date output unless a higher external governance process exists.

hardAbortGates.condition: The domain path does not exist or tier cannot be reconciled with the classification table.
The row cannot state whether the domain affects state, action, transition, hazard, observation, time accounting, policy, access, option value, governance or uncertainty.
A domain narrative is treated as a coefficient, effect size, calibrated predictor or scenario parameter without Q3/Q4 evidence.
An association, biomarker, endpoint, access metric or observational claim is interpreted as a causal intervention effect without causal design.
The bridge is used to output an individual death date, individual life expectancy, personal medical advice, treatment selection or intervention ranking.
The bridge row requires raw individual data, credentials, restricted files, personal identifiers or public AI upload of sensitive data.

nonGoals: This contract does not estimate model parameters.
This contract does not validate causal intervention effects.
This contract does not open aggregate calibrated research modeling.
This contract does not support individual prediction, individual death dates, medical advice or intervention ranking.
